high_water.shared_prompt: Use case: lighting-weather. Input image 1 is the edit target, a 2-column x 3-row atlas from a Korean pixel-art first-person survival game. Make its later FLOOD SURGE state. Treat the existing architecture and every camera as a locked plate. Preserve exactly the same six horizontal panoramas, identical camera eye position, perspective, rooms, object placement, pixel-art style, grid seams at x=50%, y=1/3 and 2/3. Keep the lower right refuge tile dry. Change the WATER ITSELF visibly enough for a player to tell the water has risen even in a still thumbnail: real waterlines against recognizable solids, grounded physical ripples, more energetic rainfall outdoors, cooler reflected light. Calm upper grounds stay plausible. Day/evening remains the same. Absolutely no new text, borders, UI, watermarks, people or floating icons. Specific water changes by cell:

maps.flood-home: Top-left a layer of noticeably deeper blue-grey floodwater now laps against all four low table legs and the bottom of bedding, reflecting the household lamp and window; preserve the furniture and the ceiling-height window. Top-right the communal entrance fills with water submerging bottom exterior steps, reflecting amber wall lamp, with higher inner landing above it. Middle-left lower concrete steps are underwater, remaining upper treads visible/dry. Middle-right water pushes down the downhill gutter outside the higher corner shop under heavy rain, its sill remains clear. Bottom-left a broad runnel moves across the base of the school approach while the raised school gate and entrance stand clear. Bottom-right shelter mats remain dry, near-identical.
maps.flood-work: Top-left view from duty desk and monitors stays in place, through the glass newly deeper floodwater covering the lower part of the concourse columns; keep desk above water. Top-right choppy sheet of real dark water reaches partway up the metal ticket-gate bases, yellow strip mostly obscured, amber and green reflections stretched. Middle-left water extends down service corridor to the base of wall cabinet, pipes and window unchanged. Middle-right foreground elevated railing and intercom remain above water, but down below broad floodwater and swirling reflections are easy to see. Bottom-left standing at same lower landing looking up to surface exit, lowest few stair treads now underwater, upper stair flight clear. Bottom-right ground-level shelter/assembly point stays unchanged.
maps.flood-travel: Top-left from the same orange tent: a fast much higher, wider jade-grey river with strong whitewater swallows the lower halves of the same boulders and reaches the bank at the edge of the tent, leave tent recognizably in place. Top-right water now rushes close to the base of the original posts below the ranger kiosk and trail. Middle-left rising torrent almost reaches the outer edge of the pavilion deck, bright foam and spray against visible timber posts; the benches stay above it. Middle-right same high rocky overlook, a much wider whitewater channel in the valley far below, heavy rain, foreground high trail intact. Bottom-left same ridge shelter gate, runoff trickling down step edges and heavier rain, no physical river on the high mountain. Bottom-right the dry warm shelter remains unchanged.

shared_prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE professional videogame environment sprite atlas for one map: a perfectly regular edge-to-edge 2-COLUMN by 3-ROW rectangular grid, SIX distinct ultrawide landscape shots. Overall canvas landscape 3:2; each tile is panorama 2.25:1. Hard cuts exactly at the 50% width and 1/3 and 2/3 heights. Absolutely no gutters, dividers, outlines, margin, frames, labels, characters, typography, lettering, HUD, or watermark. Each tile will be cut apart and used full screen independently. Every view is FIRST-PERSON eye height, standing at the named place in contemporary South Korea; close physical surfaces at frame edges, a strong center-midground landmark, depth and readable route silhouettes. Grounded, atmospheric adventure-game background art: hand-placed crisp 1990s pixel clusters and selective dithering, moody petroleum shadows, luminous practical lights, richly observed architecture, distinctive pixels, restrained color. Keep important scenery near the horizontal middle of each tile so it can crop on mobile. Keep the left-bottom edge quiet for an independently drawn caption. No player, hands, caricature, visible injury or lettering. Consecutive locations share weather and visual motifs, but MUST read as six different places with six different compositions. Camera stays inside each environment, no overhead map, no cutaway building. Compose in this exact reading order top-left, top-right, middle-left, middle-right, bottom-left, bottom-right:

maps.flood-home: A Korean hillside neighborhood during a blue-hour downpour; teal reflected water, amber house lights, brick walls. (1) INSIDE a lived-in banjiha half-basement studio living room; decisive ground-level high horizontal street window at ceiling height, shoes of street passers not needed, low table and folded bedding, a wavering sheet of water under the threshold. (2) A narrow tiled semi-basement shared entrance passage with wall-mounted mailboxes, rain dripping by the outer threshold; camera faces the split-level landing. (3) Looking up a tight U-turn concrete indoor stair from a half landing; simple metal handrail, warm amber window and higher dry treads. (4) At a higher, open neighborhood alley bend, under an eave, a shuttered corner grocery, small white street loudspeaker mounted near a pole, rain running down the gutter. (5) Standing on a school entrance ramp and looking through its open metal gate toward a lit doorway, yellow hatching and stone walls. (6) INSIDE the school assembly hall being used as a shelter: wooden court, neatly spaced sleeping mats, dry windows showing rain, warm welcoming light.
maps.flood-work: A Korean metro station during monsoon flooding; turquoise-blue tile band and amber light visually tie each stage together. (1) Standing just inside the small station duty office, looking across the duty desk, radio charging cradle and control monitors to a wet tiled concourse through glass. (2) A row of stainless steel station ticket gates with a yellow tactile stripe, thin shallow reflections under flickering fluorescent light, eye-level inside gate hall. (3) Narrow glazed crew passage outside a storage cabinet, painted turquoise stripe, pipes, tiled floor. (4) At an elevated mezzanine, glass and metal railing overlooking the wet concourse, staff intercom post and ceiling-mounted loudspeaker. (5) Looking up a broad station exit staircase from its half landing to a gray rainy street, bands of daylight coming from above. (6) From under a dry civic awning at a street-level assembly square above the station entrance: small rescue canopy, folding chairs, rain in the distance. No train-track access or people wading.
maps.flood-travel: A Korean mountain valley in heavy summer rain, moss-green granite, milky jade torrent, burnt-orange camping details, no tropical jungle. The camera stands on land in every scene. (1) Under the flysheet of a tiny riverside campsite on a bank, tent flap in the near foreground, swollen boulder stream filling the midground, soft gray sky. (2) At the timber ranger information kiosk beside a rocky trail, roof eaves frame the swollen stream below; a hard case beside the service shelf. (3) On the deck of a covered timber picnic pavilion, benches and a handrail above water-struck boulders, tiled eaves. (4) A high forest trail lookout: a narrow dry switchback, marker post, bench and iron railing at the cliff, white water far below. (5) At the entrance gate of a ridge-side mountain shelter reached by granite steps; a timber lintel, pine trees and warm porch light. (6) INSIDE the mountain visitor shelter, rough timber walls, shelves of neatly folded blankets and dry boots by a stove; rainy valley seen through a small window.
maps.fire-home: Evening in a Korean apartment complex during a building fire, smoked amber light, desaturated greens, localized smoke and alarm lights, not every room burning. (1) Inside a lived-in Korean apartment living room; low sofa, tea cups on the dining table, sliding balcony windows through which orange light reaches the ceiling. (2) Long apartment access corridor seen at standing height, repeated numbered-less apartment doors on one side, square ventilation openings, warm smoky vanishing point and small red alarm lamp. (3) Close concrete emergency stair landing; slanted steel rail in foreground, small wired-glass window, amber edge light. (4) Walking into the paved forecourt of a low apartment management office; its ground-floor service window faces us, concrete planter on right and smoke high in the distant sky. (5) The narrow pedestrian gate out of the complex seen up close, gateposts, brick pillars, a path toward an open square. (6) In the broad open assembly plaza beyond the apartments; simple pavement, bench, emergency canopy, distant smoky residential blocks. The last scene feels open and calm.
maps.fire-work: Fire at dusk in a Korean office building. Smoke hangs near ceilings, outside glows orange, green-gray offices, red alarm fixtures, survivable human scale. (1) Standing between office desks on the fourth floor, monitor backs, swivel chairs, low suspended ceiling, an orange-lit window behind a desk. (2) Inside the EAST enclosed stair with a prominent red emergency cabinet and yellow painted metal stairs, narrow and warmly lit. (3) Inside the WEST concrete stair, cool blue wired-glass window, gray steel rail and a low metal cabinet, sharply different view down a diagonal landing. (4) Second-floor landing directly beside a tall gridded window, a small radio call point on the wall, dim skyline visible. (5) Ground-floor lobby with glass exit and green pictogram light, big dark floor mat looking out to the assembly plaza. (6) From the open paved assembly area across the road: office building in the distance, parked rescue vehicle and a metal barrier, open smoky evening sky.
maps.fire-travel: At a modest Korean coastal hotel during a night fire; dark indigo shadows, amber lamp pools, slight smoke and alarm glows. (1) From inside a small hotel guestroom, rumpled duvet, open travel bag, heavy curtain catching smoky sunset and a half-open hallway door. (2) Compact guest lounge with two low curved sofas facing the broad glass hotel facade and low tables under a floor lamp. (3) In the service corridor outside the laundry: linen trolley near camera, circular washer doors visible beyond open utility door, cool tile and a red alarm reflection. (4) Inside a staff waiting hall with lockers, bench, wall intercom, counter, warm emergency fixture. (5) In a tall front lobby facing glass exit doors, reception counter on right, pavement and small fountain beyond. (6) Standing in an open coastal hotel square under blue night sky, tiled plaza, distant hotel with a smoky upper wing, emergency beacon reflections; quiet safe ending.
maps.quake-home: A Korean residential apartment complex in dusty ochre late-afternoon light immediately after an earthquake. Moderate believable displacement, small plaster and dust, structure still legible. (1) Inside a Korean family living room, low table and colored pencils on floor, slightly tilted hanging frame, thin shaft of sunlight picking dust. (2) At eye height in a narrow apartment corridor beside a slightly tilted floor marker pictogram, shoes by a front door and chipped plaster. (3) Looking across the common concrete stairwell, metal balustrade in foreground, window frame holding sunlit grit. (4) In the inner paved apartment courtyard with a flagpole and a low hedge, residential wings enclose it. (5) At the fenced playground entrance, close colorful swing frame beyond the opening and a path to an open lot. (6) In the open neighborhood assembly lot, broad bare ground and a distant apartment skyline in still evening light, scattered folded blankets.
maps.quake-work: A contemporary Korean neighborhood library in muted honey and charcoal, immediately after an earthquake, fine plaster dust suspended in daylight. (1) Inside the upstairs library reading room at desk height, fallen hardcover books on the floor, shelves and tall windows. (2) Main library stair beside a wooden information desk, rolling stacks behind, dust and brass-colored handrail. (3) Narrow concrete annex stairwell with a metal service drawer, different cooler light and high dusty windows. (4) Standing in a spacious open library courtyard, modest flag on the far wall, library wing on the left, dust catching the sun. (5) At a school sports ground gate, track beyond and a pair of low guidance lamps at the entrance; dusty ground. (6) From the middle of an open athletics field, soft track curve, far-away low school and library blocks, broad warm sky. No fire or flood.
maps.quake-travel: A small Korean mountain railway station after an earthquake; weathered bottle-green ironwork, old brick, cool daylight and pale ochre dust. (1) Inside the passenger waiting room, rows of metal chairs, a dark information board above, loose paper timetables blowing across the floor; no readable text. (2) Close to vintage ticket counter windows with service openings, stool and swinging hanging lamp behind glass. (3) In the luggage storage room, stacked metal lockers with keys and suitcases at eye level, thin dusty daylight. (4) Inside the station's open brick forecourt, a small emergency flag near a planter, terminal wall on one side. (5) In a covered pedestrian passage leading straight to the station square, green cast iron columns, guiding inset lights and warm daylight beyond. (6) Standing in the wide empty station assembly plaza; the small station, hills and a rescue tent in the distance, grounded and quiet.
